name: trait TrustedRandomAccess : TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce
rule: If Self implements Iterator, implementors of TrustedRandomAccess must ensure that, after __iterator_get_unchecked(&mut self, idx), it remains safe to call Clone::clone, Iterator::size_hint, DoubleEndedIterator::next_back, ExactSizeIterator::len, Iterator::__iterator_get_unchecked, and TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce::size on self when the required traits are implemented, provided all of these conditions hold: 0 <= idx < self.size(); if Self does not implement Clone, the same index is never requested on self more than once; after the unchecked access, next_back() is called at most self.size() - idx - 1 times, with this limit calculated separately for self and each clone but counting next_back() calls before cloning against both; after the unchecked access, only those listed methods are called on self or any new clones. Coercion from Self to any supertype T is permitted, including multiple successive coercions; after an unchecked access, the same method restriction applies to every resulting coerced value, and the same-index unchecked-access counts and next_back() counts are summed across self and successive coercion results and must remain within the stated bounds.
expression: The supplied grammar cannot express this requirement. It exposes only opaque `$1`, with no trait predicates or temporal call, clone, or coercion histories.
